acceptance.given: A Matrix aggregate is evaluated with its required case-and-subject execution set, with one required execution deliberately absent.

oracle.expected: The aggregate result is failed and identifies incomplete required execution coverage.
forbidden: A passing aggregate result despite the missing execution.
Ignoring the missing Matrix Case or subject execution.
oracle.observable: The aggregate receipt/status returned by the replay-matrix evaluation.

acceptance.then: The missing required execution prevents aggregate success.
acceptance.when: The Matrix aggregate evaluator assesses required Matrix Case execution coverage.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the planned S41 aggregate-evaluation test with a Matrix fixture that omits one required case-and-subject execution.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make aggregate evaluation fail closed whenever its required Matrix Case and subject execution coverage is incomplete.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: The aggregate receipt remains backward-compatible; rollback restores the prior evaluator behavior without changing historical evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: Aggregate evaluation with incomplete required coverage transitions to failed rather than successful.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Aggregate success is emitted only after every required Matrix Case input and both-subject execution is present; any omission emits failure.

acceptance.given: An applicable Consumer has a recorded Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline before enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable.

oracle.expected: After the full real-call-surface sequence, the observed Route identity equals the recorded Prior Route identity and both verdict and diagnostics equal their recorded baseline.
forbidden: Prior Route identity is not restored.
The verdict baseline is not restored.
The diagnostic baseline is not restored.
oracle.observable: The Consumer sequence result and its post-sequence Route identity, verdict, and diagnostics.

acceptance.then: The Consumer is restored to its prior route and verdict/diagnostic baseline.
acceptance.when: The Consumer executes enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable through its real call surface.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the planned S41 Consumer sequence test with a route or baseline restoration mismatch.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Execute each applicable Consumer through enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable, and compare the final route identity, verdict, and diagnostics to its captured Prior Route baseline.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback preserves existing Consumer route and receipt formats and restores the prior route-selection behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: A Consumer with a captured prior baseline returns to that exact identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline after the complete sequence.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: For every applicable Consumer, the post-re-enable Route identity, verdict, and diagnostics exactly match its pre-sequence Prior Route baseline.

acceptance.given: An aggregate execution is configured to produce output under its finite output limit.

oracle.expected: The aggregate enforces its configured finite output limit and its emitted output remains at or below that limit.
forbidden: An aggregate produces output without a finite bound.
oracle.observable: The aggregate execution configuration and the measured or recorded output-limit result.

acceptance.then: The aggregate remains within its configured finite output bound.
acceptance.when: An aggregate executes and produces output.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the planned S11 bound-enforcement test against an aggregate configuration with no finite output bound or output exceeding its configured bound.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Apply a finite output budget to aggregate execution and make budget exhaustion deterministically unsuccessful.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback retains the existing aggregate receipt shape and deterministic unsuccessful terminal state for exhausted budgets.

slice_hint.state_transition: A running aggregate transitions to a bounded successful result within its limit or an unsuccessful terminal result when the output budget is exhausted.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: No aggregate execution can produce unbounded output; configured output-budget exhaustion has an unsuccessful deterministic terminal state.

acceptance.given: A historical replay binding is recorded and the supplied replay inputs resolve to a different binding identity.

oracle.expected: Verification first reconstructs the original recorded binding identity, attempts replay only with that same identity, and rejects the replay when the supplied inputs do not match it.
forbidden: Accepting a replay with mismatched historical binding identities.
Treating mismatched replay inputs as the historically bound inputs.
oracle.observable: The historical replay validation result, including reconstructed original identity, supplied replay identity, and rejection status.

acceptance.then: The historical replay identity mismatch is rejected.
acceptance.when: Historical replay inputs are validated against their recorded binding.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the planned S36 replay-binding test with replay inputs whose reconstructed identity differs from the recorded historical binding.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reconstruct the original historical replay binding identity before replay, require the same-identity replay inputs, and reject any identity mismatch.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback preserves historical records as non-authorizing evidence and does not alter recorded binding identities or receipt compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: A replay candidate with a nonmatching reconstructed historical binding identity transitions to rejected rather than accepted.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Verification reconstructs the original binding identity first, replays only with that same identity, and rejects every identity mismatch.
